Societal Evolution Ladder
These distinct stages represent a normal progression of human
social evolution, mirroring early development in the Old World.
Middle Barbarism
Apex agricultural societies with complex urban centers.
(Examples: Aztecs, Incas, Mayas).
Lower Barbarism
Semi-agricultural tribes with established villages.
(Examples: Iroquois, Algonquins, Sioux).
Upper Savagery
Nomadic tribes, hunters, and gatherers. (Examples:
Tierra del Fuegans, Columbia River Basin tribes).

The Americas were not a static museum of primitive life. They were a dynamic,
evolving civilization actively transitioning out of communalism and organizing into
early class-based states. The conquest did not bring civilization to a wilderness;
it violently interrupted an indigenous evolution already well underway.

The history of the Americas is not a
tale of discovering an empty world.
It is the epic drama of two distinct
economic systems colliding.
The Americas provided the unimaginable material
wealth that fueled the rise of global capitalism.
Indigenous societies were complex, democratic,
and dynamically evolving.
The violent conquest laid the groundwork for the
modern class struggles of the Western Hemisphere.
